demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The shell, in the kit, with PROJECT, REGION, NUMBER, API and tok from the block above. Steps 4 to 7 run offline at Rs 0 and need no project: the first make agent-turn or make agent-eval builds ~/graph-venv with the chat image's pins (lesson 5.4 may have made it already), which takes a few minutes once. Step 3 uses the chat service on your lane; steps 8 and 9 call gemini-3.6-flash on location global and rag-api's /v1/passages as documind-ui-sa. The bench's desk searches by class, and drops every passage that has none (services/chat/desk_agent.py, _search()). Lesson 10.4 gives each document its class, and this lesson comes first, so run its one line now: it writes acme's and zeta's registries from evals/manifest.json and relabels their stored rows, as lesson 10.4 explains. A second run finds nothing to change. It ends with a relabel_applied line for each company; an exit status of 3 means BigQuery deferred a statement, and its last line says to run it again later. A pin_miss in its plan means the object on your lane is not the version the manifest records, and lesson 10.4 shows how a person re-pins it.

question: I earn Rs 52,000 a month and leave after 7 years 8 months. What gratuity is due?

model call 1 (thinking low): in 267, thinking 64, visible 21 tokens, Rs 0.0882
  -> retrieve(query="gratuity fifteen days wages for every completed year of service")
       5 passages
         [1] payment_of_gratuity_act_1972.pdf (statute)
         [2] code_on_social_security_2020.pdf (statute)
         [3] code_on_social_security_2020.pdf (statute)
         [4] labour_codes_compliance_handbook.pdf (guidance)
         [5] labour_codes_compliance_handbook.pdf (guidance)
model call 2 (thinking low): in 2,329, thinking 64, visible 17 tokens, Rs 0.3486
  -> gratuity_estimate(monthly_wage=52000, years=7, months=8)
       = Rs 2,40,000: 7 years 8 months counts as 8 years (a part of a year over six months counts as a year); Rs 52,000 / 26 x 15 x 8 = Rs 2,40,000
model call 3 (thinking low): in 2,840, thinking 64, visible 10 tokens, Rs 0.4093
  -> no tool: the answer

answer, as the Desk shows it (the model's text, then what code writes):
  Gratuity, an estimate: Rs 2,40,000 [2].

  Worked out in code:
  - Gratuity, an estimate (Code on Social Security, 2020, s.53(1), s.53(2), s.53 Explanation 3, s.53(3)): 7 years 8 months counts as 8 years (a part of a year over six months counts as a year); Rs 52,000 / 26 x 15 x 8 = Rs 2,40,000. The monthly wage from your message; the years from your message; the months from your message. An estimate, not the amount owed: the wages are the monthly rate last drawn as given; a better term in an award, agreement or contract wins (s.53(5)); a forfeiture under s.53(6) is not counted. No ceiling is applied: s.53(3) caps gratuity at an amount the Central Government notifies, which these documents do not hold.

demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: At lesson end: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The pin back is a separate window on purpose: pasted together with the line above, it would put acme straight back on RAG Engine before the lesson began. Leave it until the lesson's last step is done.
